blinding: Raters see the task requirements and a randomized artifact only. They do not see the language arm, provider, model, generation parameters, token/cost data, or other raters' scores.

requirement_coverage.1: Misses the core requested behavior or produces an unusable result.
requirement_coverage.2: Implements only part of the core behavior; major stated requirements are absent.
requirement_coverage.3: Implements the core behavior, with a material omission or brittle edge case.
requirement_coverage.4: Covers all stated requirements with only a minor, non-blocking gap.
requirement_coverage.5: Covers every stated requirement and handles the declared edge cases clearly.

clarity.1: Intent and control flow are difficult to infer; names or structure obscure behavior.
clarity.2: Several important steps require careful reconstruction or undocumented assumptions.
clarity.3: The main flow is understandable, but some names, boundaries, or failure paths are unclear.
clarity.4: The flow, names, and failure handling are straightforward to review.
clarity.5: The artifact communicates purpose and behavior directly, with no needless complexity.

changeability.1: A small declared change would require a rewrite or risks breaking unrelated behavior.
changeability.2: The change would touch several tightly coupled sections and is difficult to test safely.
changeability.3: The change is feasible but needs multiple edits or lacks a clear verification point.
changeability.4: The likely change is localized and can be checked with the supplied tests.
changeability.5: The design exposes a clear change point and a direct regression check.

adjudication: Two independent blinded raters score each artifact. If any dimension differs, a third blinded rater independently scores all dimensions; those scores are the resolved scores. Preserve all three ratings.
